title: Structural effect on NIR luminescence of three salen type heteropolynuclear 3d–4f erbium complexes

synthesis.procedure: To a stirred solution of H2L (0.2 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (10 ml) was added a solution of Er(OAc)3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) in CH3OH (10 ml). The mixture was stirred for 4 h at room temperature, the clear yellow solution was filtered, and diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature. Crystals suitable for single-crystal X-ray analysis were obtained in 7 days.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; diethyl ether diffused slowly into the filtrate at room temperature; X-ray-quality crystals in 7 days

properties.summary: Solid-state NIR emission at 298 K (λex = 466 nm) shows Er3+ 4I13/2 → 4I15/2 bands from 1400–1650 nm with maxima at 1530 nm. Visible ligand emission is complementary in intensity to the NIR bands. Monoexponential NIR lifetime τ = 2.68 μs; NIR intensity order is 2 > 1 > 3. UV–vis in CH3CN (1×10−5 mol L−1) is ligand-like with a red-shifted shoulder upon coordination.

synthesis.procedure: To a stirred solution of H2L (0.2 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (10 ml) was added Er(OAc)3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) in CH3OH (10 ml). After stirring 4 h at room temperature, NH4PF6 (0.4 mmol) was added and the mixture was stirred a further 8 h at room temperature. The solution was filtered and diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature. Crystals suitable for single-crystal X-ray analysis were obtained in 7 days.

properties.summary: Strongest NIR emitter among 1–3 in the solid state at 298 K (order 2 > 1 > 3), attributed to two salen ligands shielding Er3+ and a near-linear Zn–Er–Zn arrangement. NIR maximum at 1530 nm (λex = 466 nm) with the longest monoexponential lifetime of the series (τ = 3.42 μs). UV–vis remains ligand-centered with a coordination-induced red shift.

properties.summary: Weakest NIR emitter of 1–3 in the solid state at 298 K, attributed to four coordinated methanol ligands and ten acetates that quench Er3+ NIR emission. Still shows the characteristic 1530 nm 4I13/2 → 4I15/2 band (λex = 466 nm) with the shortest lifetime of the series (τ = 1.84 μs).
